strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Prevents scheduled recovery from reviving terminal product-complete stops while preserving recovery task admission for concrete product-loop interruption faults.
Rust classifies persisted stop evidence before admission and revalidates recovery provenance at direct task.run before TaskRunning.
Typed bounded TaskRecord provenance and TaskStarted evidence expose the recovery boundary to headless callers without raw content.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with runtime_permission_enforcement and persistent_structured_ledger support.
answers.new_capability: A terminal product-complete drive stop cannot become a recovery task, while a recoverable product_continuation_checkpoint_missing stop can admit one provenance-bound recovery task that direct task.run revalidates before TaskRunning.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M60.1 admitted broad stop reasons and stored no typed product-loop stop recovery provenance on TaskRecord, so direct task.run had no point-of-use stop evidence freshness check.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled controller could revive a completed product loop or run an admitted recovery task after the source stop boundary became stale or terminal.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M59.1 drive sequencing and M60.1 stop recovery admission because this phase changes stop classification and direct-run provenance invariants rather than adding another route or wrapper.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing headless.continue_once and task.run behavior changes; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The runtime persists typed bounded provenance and existing bounded results are sufficient; no report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime classifies drive-stop evidence as recoverable, terminal, or budget-exhausted before task creation, persists product-loop stop recovery provenance, and revalidates it before direct task.run can append TaskRunning.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can recover from interruption-like product-loop stops without sacrificing finite terminal completion semantics or relying on caller-side stop interpretation.
answers.milestone_progress: Repairs the M60 recovery boundary so M60 can safely proceed to a dedicated run route or close out if direct execution is sufficient.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: Manifest changes select and describe M60.1.1; guard engine logic is unchanged.

exit_criteria: Runtime classifies product-loop drive-stop evidence before recovery task creation
stop_autonomous_development and product-complete terminal evidence are denied before recovery task creation
product_continuation_checkpoint_missing remains admissible as a recoverable fault when fingerprints and sequence match
admitted recovery tasks persist typed product_loop_stop_recovery_provenance on TaskRecord and TaskStarted evidence
direct task.run revalidates current source stop evidence before TaskRunning and denies stale or terminal provenance without execution side effects
existing duplicate-boundary and exact replay behavior remains duplicate-free
behavior_evidence: Behavior test headless_continue_admits_product_loop_stop_recovery_from_drive_evidence_and_replays validates recoverable admission, typed provenance, replay without duplicate task/event creation, terminal stop denial, stale evidence denial, authorization denial, and direct task.run stale-provenance denial before TaskRunning.
Validation includes targeted cargo check and the Rust behavior test for recoverable admission, terminal denial, typed provenance, replay, and stale direct-run denial.

accepted_capability: Runtime distinguishes terminal product-complete stop evidence from recoverable product-loop interruption evidence before recovery admission.
Admitted product-loop stop recovery tasks carry typed TaskRecord provenance that direct task.run revalidates before TaskRunning.
behavior_evidence: Behavior test headless_continue_admits_product_loop_stop_recovery_from_drive_evidence_and_replays covers terminal stop denial, recoverable admission, typed provenance, exact replay, duplicate-boundary denial, stale target denial, authorization denial, and stale direct-run denial before TaskRunning.
safety_boundary: Recovery admission requires explicit product_loop_stop_recovery authorization and current persisted drive-stop evidence.
Terminal product-complete and budget-exhausted stops fail closed before task creation.
Direct task.run denies product-loop stop recovery tasks when current stop evidence no longer matches provenance or is no longer recoverable.
Ledger and task records store bounded ids, labels, sequence numbers, and SHA-256 fingerprints only.
non_goals: Does not add the M60.2 recovery execution route.
Does not add a JSON-RPC method, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary wrapper.
Does not run provider, tools, workspace apply, shell, git, network, or services during recovery admission.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected preserving no_eligible_product_continuation_route as broadly recoverable because M59 can emit it for terminal stop_autonomous_development decisions.
Rejected adding a stop-inspection wrapper because it would not enforce admission or direct-run invariants.
Rejected making only a future M60.2 route safe because direct task.run would remain a caller bypass.
technical_debt: The explicit next route still uses the existing run-product-continuation route kind while next_action identifies recovery execution; a later phase can add a dedicated route if it materially changes execution semantics.
next_capability_rationale: After M60.1.1, evaluate whether a dedicated M60.2 recovery-run route adds capability beyond the now-safe direct task.run path.
